title: Burns and scalds
scenario: Skin burned by fire, hot metal, boiling water, or steam. Burnt hand on a stove, hot pan, or iron. Red, blistering, or charred skin, scald from hot liquid.
steps: Move the person away from the heat source.
Cool under running water for 20 minutes as soon as possible. Cool the burn, not the person.
Remove rings, watches, and tight clothing near the burn before it swells — but leave anything stuck to the skin.
Cover loosely with a clean, non-fluffy cloth or plastic wrap.
Call 911 if the burn is larger than the person's palm, on the face, hands, feet, or groin, caused by chemicals or electricity, or the person is a young child or elderly.
do_not: Do not put ice, butter, creams, oils, or toothpaste on a burn.
Do not pull off clothing stuck to the burn.
